privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.telemetry: This HTML5 speed test server is configured with telemetry enabled.
privacy.collect-intro: At the end of the test, the following data is collected and stored:
privacy.item.results: Test results (download and upload speed, ping and jitter)
privacy.item.location: Approximate location (inferred from IP address, not GPS)
privacy.use-intro: Data collected through this service is used to:
privacy.use.share: Allow sharing of test results (sharable image for forums, etc.)
privacy.use.improve: To improve the service offered to you (for instance, to detect problems on our side)
privacy.no-disclosure: No personal information is disclosed to third parties.
privacy.consent: By starting the test, you consent to the terms of this privacy policy.
privacy.removal: If you want to have your information deleted, you need to provide either the ID of the test or your IP address. This is the only way to identify your data, without this information we won't be able to comply with your request.
privacy.contact: Contact this email address for all deletion requests:
conn.single-title: Single connection: one in each direction, what a regular download achieves
conn.multi-title: Multiple connections: 6 for the download and 3 for the upload, the full capacity of the link

history.server-note: This server also keeps every speed test it receives (see the privacy policy). Clearing this history does not delete them.

route.back.intro: A web page cannot trace this route, so run the command below on your computer and paste what it prints. The text is read here, in your browser.

route.back.clip-linux: On Linux this uses xclip; with Wayland, use wl-copy in its place.

route.back.drop-hint: You can also drop a .txt file with the output on the box.

route.back.privacy: When you press Show my route or Paste and show, or when your browser extension hands over a route, only the public addresses of the routers (never your internal network) are sent to this server, to look up their network and country. They are not saved; only a keyed hash of your own address is kept, for up to an hour, to limit how often this can be asked.

privacy.route: Route page: when you press Start, your IP address is given to a command on this server that sends test packets to it. The result is shown only to you and is not stored on the server; your browser keeps your latest routes (Route history) until you clear them. To limit how often routes are traced, a keyed hash of your address is kept for up to a minute.
privacy.route-back: Route page, your route to the server: the text you paste is read in your browser. When you press Show my route, only the public addresses of the routers are sent to this server to look up their network and country; they are not stored, and your internal addresses never leave the browser. To limit how often this can be asked, a keyed hash of your address and the times of your requests are kept for up to an hour.
